products.name: Managed Identities for Azure Logic Apps & Functions — Authenticating to Microsoft 365 Without Stored Credentials — Commercial
products.short_description: Stop storing service-account passwords and secrets in your automations — authenticate Azure Logic Apps and Functions to Microsoft 365 with managed identities and application permissions.
products.description:
Stop storing service-account passwords and secrets in your automations — authenticate Azure Logic Apps and Functions to Microsoft 365 with managed identities and application permissions.

Automations that reach into Microsoft 365 too often run on a stored service-account connection or a client secret sitting in the workflow — credentials that must be rotated, can leak, and grant standing access. Managed identities remove the credential entirely: Azure issues and rotates it, and you grant it exactly the app permissions it needs. This solution is the pattern reference for authenticating Azure Logic Apps and Functions to Microsoft 365 (Graph and related resources) with managed identities — system-assigned vs user-assigned and when to use each, granting application permissions / app-role assignments to the identity, calling Graph from Logic Apps and from Functions, and migrating existing secret-based flows off stored credentials.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • System- vs user-assigned — how each works, when to choose which, and how a shared user-assigned identity simplifies multi-workflow estates
  • Grant the right access — assigning application Graph permissions / app roles to a managed identity, least-privilege by default (points to #4 for mailbox scoping)
  • Call Graph from Logic Apps — the managed-identity authentication action and common Graph calls, no connector, no secret
  • Call Graph from Azure Functions — DefaultAzureCredential / managed-identity token flow in code, with a working example
  • Migrate off secrets — a repeatable path from stored service-account/secret connections to managed identity, with a validation script inventorying which workflows still use credentials

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

A credential-free authentication standard for your Azure automations — Logic Apps and Functions reaching Microsoft 365 through managed identities and least-privilege app permissions, with a migration path off stored secrets.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • MIM365-Discovery.ps1 — inventory Azure Logic Apps and Function Apps, whether each has a managed
    • MIM365-Find-StoredCredentials.ps1 — report Logic Apps / Function Apps still using stored
    • MIM365-Report.ps1 — identity/permission inventory across the estate, exported to CSV
    • MIM365-Set-AppRole.ps1 — assign (or verify) a least-privilege application app-role on Microsoft
    • MIM365-Validate.ps1 — PASS/FAIL check that a target Logic App / Function App has a managed

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all five PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
